findings.F1: Where a coin's close sits in its own 20-day high-low range predicts its next 10 days better than the tested 30-day return does: the slope of the de-drifted 10-day return on the range position is +1.22 % per standard deviation (t 3.98, 2699 non-overlapping cases), against +0.78 % (t 2.44, 2411 cases) for the 30-day return. The slope is +0.70 % (t 3.48, 2843 cases) over 5 days and +1.15 % (t 3.62) for the 30-day range.
findings.F2: The range position takes over the 30-day momentum: in a joint regression on the 10-day de-drifted return, the 30-day range position keeps its slope (+1.17 %, t 2.67) while the 30-day return loses its own (-0.03 %, t -0.06).
findings.F3: The effect sits at the top of the range. In the top fifth of the 30-day range position, a coin beats its normal 10-day drift by +2.67 % (t 2.95, 485 cases), about 14 times the 0.19 % cost of a round trip. The second-lowest fifth falls -1.41 % (t -2.24), but the lowest fifth falls only -0.13 % (t -0.19).
findings.F4: The book's gain comes from its long side alone. Before costs, the long side earns +0.090 % per coin-bar (t 5.27) and the short side -0.007 % (t -0.48). On the 5-day grid, long cells earn +0.93 % and short cells -0.11 %.
findings.F5: Within negative forecasts, the slope of the 5-day de-drifted return on the forecast is -0.43 % per standard deviation (t -1.71, 1703 cases): the deepest 30-day falls are followed by smaller declines than mild ones, so the short half of momentum does not grade. This is suggestive only, given how many angles were looked at.

ideas.idea: The nearer a coin's close is to the top of its 20-day high-low range, the more it rises over the next 10 days, beyond its normal drift.
ideas.consequence: A trader should lean long on a coin closing near the top of its recent range, more the nearer it is, and refuse longs on coins sitting low in it.
ideas.name: close near range top continues

ideas.idea: The nearer a coin's close is to the top of its 30-day high-low range, the more it rises over the next 10 days, beyond its normal drift; the move is carried by the upper part of the range.
ideas.consequence: A trader should take the long side of range strength and not rely on its mirror image (shorting the range bottom) for the same gain.
ideas.name: upper-range strength drives rises
